do_not_assume: A Data View reruns when an old communication is duplicated.
goal: A reviewed draft whose audience, sender, classification, content, consent and delivery path are ready for the organization’s approval process.
steps: Record the installed Rock version, editor surface and intended send time.
Identify the authoritative audience source and calculate its current result.
Refresh any synchronized communication-list group through its approved mechanism.
Compare source count, group count and final eligible-recipient count.
Investigate exclusions rather than adding people manually to force count alignment.
Confirm personal-versus-bulk classification.
Confirm From, Reply-To, sender domain, topic and template.
Preview representative personalization cases and every important call-to-action.
Send bounded tests to representative mailbox providers.
Confirm the transport, tracking and unsubscribe behavior.
Save as draft or submit for approval.
After authorization and sending, verify Communication History and recipient outcomes.
title: Recipe: Preflight a broad email communication

do_not_assume: Shared contact information should generate duplicate messages.
goal: A specific, evidence-backed reason the person was included, excluded or routed to a different medium.
steps: Confirm the person belongs in the authoritative targeting result.
Confirm current membership in the communication-list group.
Inspect sync state and applicable segment filters.
Inspect the person’s email address, SMS number and channel-specific eligibility.
Inspect global email preference, list subscription and medium preference.
Confirm whether the communication was personal or bulk.
Confirm duplicate prevention did not consolidate a shared destination.
Inspect the stored recipient result for the communication.
Report the exact failing layer without changing consent or contact data.
title: Recipe: Diagnose one missing recipient

do_not_assume: **Stop when:** Any layer is unverified; do not interpret missing analytics as recipient disengagement until tracking is proven.
goal: A bounded test proves Rock-to-provider handoff, inbox delivery and expected event return.
steps: Confirm the active Email medium and assigned transport.
Review transport configuration without copying secrets into notes.
Confirm the sending domain and safe-sender policy.
Confirm provider webhooks and selected tracking events.
Send a uniquely named test to a bounded recipient set.
Confirm the Rock communication and recipient records.
Confirm provider acceptance.
Confirm real inbox delivery.
Generate only the approved test events, such as an open or link click.
Confirm those events return to the corresponding Rock record.
Record which events the transport does and does not provide.
title: Recipe: Validate an email transport and its event loop

do_not_assume: An unfiltered action is harmless; it applies to every message reaching it.
goal: One controlled inbound message reaches exactly the intended conversation, reply or workflow path.
steps: Confirm the provider number and Rock System Phone Number.
Confirm the SMS transport and medium.
Confirm the webhook targets the intended endpoint or pipeline.
Review pipeline actions and filters in execution order.
Review workflow inputs and security for any workflow-launch action.
Decide whether automated replies must be saved to history.
Send one controlled inbound message.
Verify the expected conversation, reply, workflow and retained history.
Confirm no unrelated action executed.
Repeat with one negative-filter case when routing depends on keywords.
title: Recipe: Validate inbound SMS routing

do_not_assume: Flow templates and system-wide Communication Templates are interchangeable.
goal: A version-appropriate flow with a current audience, measurable goal and explicit exit behavior.
steps: Choose recurring, on-demand or one-time behavior.
Define the authoritative audience or activation event.
Define a measurable conversion goal supported by Rock.
Set the goal window and target.
Add only evidence-supported email, SMS or push messages.
Define the buffer and send time for each message.
Choose when recipients exit.
Verify consent and channel eligibility for each medium.
Test representative recipients and conversion paths.
Activate only after audience, timing and exit behavior are approved.
Monitor recipient logs, conversion and unsubscribe results.
Pause the flow if targeting or timing is wrong.
title: Recipe: Create a communication flow without over-messaging

do_not_assume: Every unsubscribe has the same cause.
goal: A bounded operational finding identifies affected audiences, senders or message patterns without over-attributing individual motives.
steps: Select a consistent date window.
Review the Unsubscribe Report by scope.
Review saturation across the same window and mediums.
Identify recurring senders, topics, lists, flows or broad communications.
Inspect classification and targeting for representative messages.
Compare provider spam complaints where available.
Separate isolated events from repeated patterns.
Recommend a concrete audience, cadence, template or training adjustment.
Measure the same reports after the change.
title: Recipe: Investigate rising unsubscribes or saturation

do_not_assume: A workflow Status label alone determines activation.
goal: One intended communication action is exercised without broadly reopening unrelated workflow work.
steps: Prefer a new test workflow instance.
If an existing marked test instance must be reused, preflight the exact recipient, action criteria, current template, action order and baseline side-effect counts.
Leave earlier setters, record-creation actions and unrelated communication actions complete.
Reopen only the target action and the minimum containing workflow state required by the reviewed procedure.
Save once through the supported Workflow Detail surface.
Inspect workflow logs and Communication History before considering any retry.
Verify exactly one intended communication, its recipient, rendered content and final workflow state.
Confirm no unrelated timestamps or records changed.
title: Recipe: Retest a workflow-backed communication safely

do_not_assume: Hiding a user-interface control removes the underlying tool, or enabling a tool bypasses Rock permissions.
goal: An agent can assist with preparation without gaining unintended send or destructive authority.
steps: List the exact communication tasks the agent needs.
Enable only the required tools.
Separate draft, preview, audience-inspection, approval and send capabilities.
Leave send disabled when the task is drafting or analysis.
Omit destructive tools unless explicitly required.
Verify the Rock identity and permissions used by the integration.
Test denied operations as well as allowed ones.
Require action-time authorization before any external send.
title: Recipe: Bound an agent that can draft communications
